claims.text: Moderate Ni doping in FeMn-based high-entropy alloys creates a more uniform local spin-exchange environment.
Moderate Ni doping enhances the low-field magnetocaloric effect in FeMn-based high-entropy alloys.
Ni doping produces minimal hysteresis in FeMn-based high-entropy alloys.
Ni doping preserves mechanical stability by hindering excessive lattice distortion or brittleness.
Fe or Mn will be systematically replaced with 0–10 at.% Ni in small increments.
Ni additions alter local spin coupling and reduce segregation of magnetic domains.
The Ni-induced magnetic changes lead to stable ferromagnetic transitions.
Localized Ni additions promote robust structural cohesion.
Ni substitution adjusts the lattice parameters and local electronic structure of FeMn-based high-entropy alloys.
Ni substitution narrows the distribution of exchange energies.
Ni substitution shifts the magnetic transition temperature.
The altered transition produces strong, reversible magnetization changes at low applied fields without large volume changes.
Ni-doped samples will have larger isothermal magnetic entropy changes than the undoped baseline at low applied fields.
Ni-doped samples will have stronger low-field magnetization than the undoped baseline.
Ni-doped samples will show minimal thermal hysteresis.
Ni-doped samples will support faster heat-exchange cycling.
Ni-doped samples will retain mechanical properties comparable or superior to those of the undoped material.
The undoped FeMn-based baseline has a moderate magnetocaloric response, higher hysteresis, and a less tunable transition temperature.
The proposed effect applies up to approximately 10 at.% Ni substitution.
Above approximately 10 at.% Ni, excessive lattice distortion may degrade magnetocaloric performance and mechanical stability.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis states that the optimal Ni concentration is unclear and that small composition changes may cause substantial deviations, but the falsification rule treats failure at any single Ni-doped composition, including potentially nonoptimal concentrations, as invalidating the entire mechanism.
